# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:config` from plugins/teamrig/config.schema.json: edit the schema, not this page. -->

Every key of a team's `<kit home>/teams/<team>/config.json`, drawn from [its JSON schema](../plugins/teamrig/config.schema.json). A key's words are its `description` there: edit them in the schema, and `npm run check` fails until `npm run docs:config` redraws this page. [Set up a team by hand](setup-by-hand.md#configuration) starts from a small config.

Values are shown as JSON; a map's keys as `*`, an array's items as `[]`.

## Top level

Team settings for the teamrig plugin. Only the roster (sessions, roles.lead) is required; every other key has a default. Unknown keys are kept as they are.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$schema` | string |  | The JSON schema this file follows, for an editor's completion and checks. |
| `configVersion` | integer (at least 1) | `1` | The config format. The CLI migrates older files and refuses to write newer ones. |
| `team` | [object](#team) |  | Where the team sits in a tree of teams. A team with no parent is the root of its own tree. teamrig team create writes it. |
| `sessions` (required) | array (unique) of [session name](#shared-types) |  | Every session id on the team, the lead included. Ids key every file and record, so they never change; a rename only appends to the team's rename log. |
| `names` | map from [session name](#shared-types) to string (matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,64}$`) | `{}` | Each session's first display and Claude Code session name, by id. A session not listed is named \<team>-\<id>. A name must be unique, never another session's id and never one Claude Code keeps for itself (main, team-lead, user, system), since a message to one never reaches a session. A rename in the team's rename log wins over it, and it keeps finding the session. |
| `leads` | map from [session name](#shared-types) to array (at least 1 item, unique) of [session name](#shared-types) | `{}` | Each sub-lead's members, by id: a sub-lead leads the sessions it lists, and roles.lead every session no sub-lead lists; a sub-lead may list sub-leads, at any depth. A session has one leader, roles.lead is never a member, and no sub-lead leads itself. Written by teamrig promote and demote. |
| `roles` (required) | [object](#roles) |  | Each role's session, by id. |
| `ownerGates` | array (at most 8 items) of string (1 to 60 characters, matching `^[^\r\n]+$`) | `["destructive data operations","product and design decisions","permissions","budget","resource changes"]` | Decision areas only the human owner can approve; silence never counts as consent for them. |
| `ruleConflicts` | array (at most 40 items) of [object](#ruleconflicts) | `[]` | Local rules (a line of a CLAUDE.md, rules file, skill, memory file, hook or settings file) kept although they conflict with a core rule, each with the side that wins. teamrig rules scan finds them; teamrig rules keep records one, teamrig rules forget drops one. The core pack lists them. |
| `messages` | [object](#messages) |  | Messages between sessions: how long one may be, and when a send to an idle session is held as a cold wake. |
| `register` | [object](#register) |  | The task list (the register): its priority levels, what each status change needs, its text limits and the thresholds of the flags teamrig check raises on tasks. |
| `skills` | [object](#skills) |  | The team's Claude Code skills: the shared area prefix, the limits teamrig check holds each skill to, and how a session lists the skills of other areas. |
| `contextFiles` | [object](#contextfiles) |  | Character budgets for the text Claude Code puts in every call's context; teamrig doctor flags a file over its budget. |
| `lock` | [object](#lock) |  | The file lock each write of the team's state files takes (the task list, the exec audit, the GitHub sync), so two writes never interleave. |
| `pushGuard` | [object](#pushguard) |  | The push guard: what a git push to a protected branch does. |
| `exec` | [object](#exec) |  | Privileged commands a reviewer approved, run once by teamrig exec run. |
| `packageGuard` | [object](#packageguard) |  | The package guard: what a Bash or PowerShell call that installs a package or runs one ad hoc does. |
| `commitGuard` | [object](#commitguard) |  | The commit guard: what a Bash or PowerShell call that runs git without the repository's hooks does. |
| `prompts` | [object](#prompts) |  | The permission prompts teamrig's own hooks raise. |
| `secretGuard` | [object](#secretguard) |  | Refuses a Bash, PowerShell, Read or Grep call that would print a secret into the session, where it stays in the transcript and every later prompt: a secret file's content, the whole environment, a secret variable's value, a Kubernetes secret's data or a dump command's output (kubectl config view --raw); and a Bash or PowerShell line that holds a secret as text (a token, credentials in a URL or an Authorization header), as the line itself stays in the transcript; and a Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit whose written text holds one, unless it writes a secret file (paths). A value handed to the tool that needs it (a pipe into docker login --password-stdin, a redirect into a file) stays allowed, and the read-only shell hook never lets such a line run without a prompt. |
| `commits` | [object](#commits) |  | The small-commits rule: one logical change per commit; a commit over either bound needs a reason line. |
| `coordinator` | [object](#coordinator) |  | The deploy coordinator: teamrig heavy runs one heavy step on the host at a time, under the host lock, teamrig merge merges a branch into its repository's default branch, teamrig deploy deploys it and teamrig claim holds deploys while a session measures; each step is recorded in the ledger. |
| `budget` | [object](#budget) |  | The weekly token budget: the pace line the team is measured against and each session's daily part of it. Usage is in weighted tokens (W) read from the session transcripts, and in % of the week from the status line when there is one. The defaults only measure and show; nothing blocks or acts. |
| `leadBoundary` | [object](#leadboundary) |  | How teamrig keeps the lead leading: its own edits, tests and code searches are nudged and shown, never blocked. |
| `loops` | [object](#loops) |  | Loop discipline inside a turn. |
| `wake` | [object](#wake) |  | Waking a session idle at its prompt when work is handed to it, instead of at its next prompt. Only work the session can go on with wakes (open or started past every task it comes after, or waiting with every wait cleared or answered), tasks handed together wake once, and each wake says what it costs. |
| `tests` | [object](#tests) |  | What teamrig test prints of a failed run. |
| `github` | [object](#github) |  | teamrig gh sync: GitHub issues read into the register as tasks of source github. It only reads GitHub and never writes to it; local tasks stay local. Each owner's repositories are read with the read-only token saved as teamrig-gh-\<owner> in the system's credential store, else the gh login (docs/github-sync.md). |
| `alerts` | [object](#alerts) |  | The alerting rule the core rules state. |
| `decisions` | [object](#decisions) |  | When the lead asks the owner the decisions waiting on them (tasks waiting on the owner's decision or approval), together in one batch instead of one at a time. A batch holds the waits not yet asked and the asked ones now past their due date; `teamrig decisions` prints it and `teamrig decisions asked` records it asked, as a meeting's start does. The lead's check says when one is due. |
| `tabStatus` | [object](#tabstatus) |  | A colored circle before each terminal tab's title for what its session is doing: green ready, yellow working (or a helper still running), orange waiting on the user, blue waiting on the user's decision (a turn whose last message has a `Decision needed:` line), red an API error, purple compacting. |
| `pickerGuard` | [object](#pickerguard) |  | Refuses Claude Code's question picker (AskUserQuestion) in every session and helper of the team, and in the lead's own thread unless the owner's daily meeting is open: the picker stops the session until the person answers, and the owner may be away for hours, so none of its other tasks moves meanwhile. The refusal tells the session to decide it when it is its own, else to record it on its task (a waiting status with its decision card, --default included), which reaches the owner through the lead, and go on with its next task; only with no task left, to end its turn with the question and a `Decision needed:` line. A helper ends its report with the decision instead. Plan mode's ExitPlanMode stays allowed. |
| `turnLog` | [object](#turnlog) |  | Each session's prompts and replies, kept in state/turn-log/\<session>/\<UTC hour>.jsonl for the task pane, so a /clear or a compaction never takes away what the person was reading in the tab. Secret shapes are redacted. |
| `readonlyShell` | [object](#readonlyshell) |  | Lets a Bash or PowerShell line run without a permission prompt when every command in it provably only reads: known readers (grep, cat, Get-Content, Select-Object...), git and kubectl reading subcommands, and no write, file redirection, command that runs code, or variable a program reads. It only ever allows: any other line gets Claude Code's own permission check. |
| `permissions` | [object](#permissions) |  | Which local allow rules stay. An allow rule in a Claude Code settings file approves a call before auto mode's classifier sees it, so a rule that approves a whole tool or a program with any arguments skips the one check that stops an injected or mistaken action. teamrig permissions trim removes the rules off keepAllow (the owner runs it with --yes); doctor flags the ones that approve a whole tool or program, or hold a credential (text in a secret's shape) that Claude Code saved with an approved command. |
| `open` | [object](#open) |  | How teamrig open starts a session in a new terminal tab. |
| `statusLine` | [object](#statusline) |  | What teamrig statusline shows beside the model and the plan's use of the week. |
| `launch` | map from [session name](#shared-types) to [object](#launch) | `{}` | Each session's Claude Code model and effort, and the folder it works in, by id: teamrig open starts it with claude --model and --effort; a session running on another model is told the /model to type at its start, and one at another effort the /effort to type at its first stop. A model or effort left unset is Claude Code's own choice, except for the lead, which starts on model opus at xhigh effort for each one it leaves unset. |
| `refresh` | [object](#refresh) |  | Context refresh: when a session finishes a task (teamrig set \<id> --status done) with its context at or over contextTokens, or with everyTasks tasks finished since its context was last fresh and the context at everyTasksMinTokens or more, or after the lead ran teamrig refresh \<session>, it writes a handover; then the user types /clear, or teamrig starts it fresh on its own (autoRestart). A relative handoverDir is resolved against the team's folder; unset, it is \<team folder>/handover. |
| `hiring` | [object](#hiring) |  | Hiring sessions with teamrig hire, each a worker the leader is sure the team needs: who decides. No cap counts hires: the host's room bounds who is at the office, and the leader decides who is hired. A hire is written into sessions, names and launch, and logged with its reason and review date; its part of the team's daily budget follows its share and queued work, like any session's. |
| `burst` | [object](#burst) |  | Bursts with teamrig burst: a time-boxed scale-out onto helpers and hired sessions that spends more of the week, for a surplus the week would leave unused at the reset or for a deadline. A person always starts one by command; nothing starts one on its own. |
| `paths` | [object](#paths) |  | Folders moved from their defaults; a relative path is resolved against the team's folder (\<kit home>/teams/\<team>). Unset, state and inbox stay under the team's folder and skills is the skills folder of Claude Code's folder ($CLAUDE\_CONFIG\_DIR, else \~/.claude). |

## `team`

Where the team sits in a tree of teams. A team with no parent is the root of its own tree. teamrig team create writes it.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | [session name](#shared-types) |  | The team's id: the name of its folder under \<kit home>/teams/. |
| `parent` | [session name](#shared-types) |  | The parent team: this team's lead reports to that team's lead. A tree has at most 3 levels, and a team at most 8 child teams. |
| `project` | string |  | The team's project folder, an absolute path: where its CLAUDE.md and rule files sit (teamrig check, doctor and rule-conflicts read them there), and where teamrig open starts its sessions unless a session's launch.\<id>.project names another. Unset, the folder holding the team's .teamrig.json pointer; doctor flags a folder that does not exist. |

## `roles`

Each role's session, by id.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lead` (required) | [session name](#shared-types) |  | Owns priorities, team rules and the owner's decision queue. |
| `coordinatorOwner` | [role holder](#shared-types) |  | Owns deploy coordination and fleet health, when the team has that role; a child team may leave it to a team above. |
| `securityReviewer` | [role holder](#shared-types) |  | Reviews the privileged commands sessions ask to run (exec), when the team has that role; the owner always may too. A child team may leave it to a team above. |

## `ruleConflicts[]`

Local rules (a line of a CLAUDE.md, rules file, skill, memory file, hook or settings file) kept although they conflict with a core rule, each with the side that wins. teamrig rules scan finds them; teamrig rules keep records one, teamrig rules forget drops one. The core pack lists them.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` (required) | string (1 to 512 characters, matching `^[^\r\n]+$`) |  | The file, \~/-relative under the user's home folder, else absolute. |
| `text` (required) | string (1 to 300 characters, matching `^[^\r\n]+$`) |  | The start of the line's text, which finds the line again when the lines above it move. |
| `rule` (required) | one of `"roles"`, `"own-change"`, `"messages"`, `"register"`, `"task-order"`, `"owner-gates"`, `"deploy"`, `"lean-calls"`, `"investigate"`, `"resources"`, `"data"`, `"contracts"`, `"skills"`, `"commits"`, `"push"`, `"worktrees"` |  | The core rule it conflicts with, by key; teamrig rules lists them by number. |
| `wins` (required) | one of `"local"`, `"teamrig"` |  | local: the local rule wins over the core rule. teamrig: the core rule wins and the local text stays, which may not always hold (removing the line is safer). |
| `reason` | string (1 to 200 characters, matching `^[^\r\n]+$`) |  | Why the user kept it, in their words. |

## `messages`

Messages between sessions: how long one may be, and when a send to an idle session is held as a cold wake.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxLines` | integer (3 to 50) | `10` | The longest message one session may send another. |
| `coldAfterMinutes` | integer (0 to 1440) | `60` | Minutes a session may sit idle before a message to it counts as a cold wake (its first call re-reads its whole context at full price). A send to a session idle this long is held once with a note to use an inbox line or send it again; 0 never holds. |

## `register`

The task list (the register): its priority levels, what each status change needs, its text limits and the thresholds of the flags teamrig check raises on tasks.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ownerSource` | [session name](#shared-types) | `"owner"` | The --source that marks a task as ordered by the human owner. |
| `priorities` | array (at least 1 item) of [object](#registerpriorities) | `[{"id":1,"name":"keep the lights on"},{"id":2,"name":"correctness"},{"id":3,"name":"scale"},{"id":4,"name":"this week's owner decisions"},{"id":5,"name":"if budget allows"}]` | The priority levels, most urgent first; a task's priority prints as p\<id>. Above them every team has teamrig's own p0, for urgent work done right now, which no config lists. Config version 1 called them tiers. |
| `goalPattern` | string (at least 1 character) |  | When set, every goal tag on a new task must match this regular expression. |
| `maxTitle` | integer (20 to 1000) | `140` | The most characters a task title may have. |
| `maxText` | integer (20 to 5000) | `300` | The most characters of a task's other text, such as its ref and notes; the title and the description have their own limits. |
| `secretPatterns` | array of string (at least 1 character) | `[]` | Extra regular expressions, matched case-insensitively, that refuse secret-looking text on top of the built-in shapes (vendor tokens, private keys, JSON web tokens, credentials in URLs, password= assignments). |
| `requireDescription` | boolean | `true` | Whether teamrig add needs --description, what the task is and why in plain words for a person, and teamrig update refuses --description none. Tasks imported from GitHub take the issue body either way. |
| `requireEvidenceOnDone` | boolean | `true` | Whether teamrig set --status done needs --evidence, unless the task already has some. |
| `requireSkillOnDone` | boolean | `true` | Whether teamrig set --status done needs --skill: the skill that holds the work's procedure, or none. |
| `requireNoteOn` | array (at most 5 items) of one of `"open"`, `"in-progress"`, `"verifying"`, `"waiting"`, `"done"`, `"dropped"` | `["waiting","verifying","done","dropped"]` | Statuses that cannot be set without a note. |
| `requireFollowupsOn` | array (at most 3 items) of one of `"verifying"`, `"done"`, `"dropped"` | `["verifying","done"]` | Statuses that cannot be set without --followups: the tasks the work leaves (a finding, a next step), or none. |
| `autoArchive` | boolean | `true` | After the first teamrig compact, a write that leaves the task list's log over 512 KiB archives it and says so in a NOTE line. false: only teamrig compact archives it. |
| `requireDecisionCard` | boolean | `true` | Whether teamrig set --status waiting on the owner's decision or approval needs a decision card (--question, --options, --recommend, --default), so the owner decides from it alone. |
| `requireProofOnVerifying` | boolean | `true` | Whether teamrig set --status verifying needs --proof, what will prove the shipped change works, and --waits naming when it runs: a time, or a task in progress or verifying. |
| `verifyGate` | one of `"refuse"`, `"warn"` | `"refuse"` | teamrig set --status in-progress while a task it needs (--after, or --waits task:) is verifying: refuse it, or warn and start it. Either way the verifying task's owner gets one inbox line a day about it. |
| `maxVerifying` | integer (0 to 100) | `5` | A session holding more verifying tasks than this is a PILE-UP in teamrig check; 0 turns the flag off. |
| `maxReparks` | integer (0 to 20) | `2` | How many times in a row a verifying task's proof may be put off to other waits; past it teamrig set --status verifying with other waits is refused and teamrig check flags REPARKED. 0 turns both off. |
| `check` | [object](#registercheck) |  | The thresholds of the flags teamrig check raises on tasks. |
| `review` | [object](#registerreview) |  | How teamrig asks for a bug's review. |

## `register.priorities[]`

The priority levels, most urgent first; a task's priority prints as p\<id>. Above them every team has teamrig's own p0, for urgent work done right now, which no config lists. Config version 1 called them tiers.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` (required) | integer (1 to 99) |  | The level's number: a task prints it as p\<id>, and 1 is the most urgent a config names (0 is teamrig's own p0). |
| `name` (required) | string (at least 1 character) |  | What the level holds, in a few words. |

## `register.check`

The thresholds of the flags teamrig check raises on tasks.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `staleAfterHours` | integer (at least 1) | `72` | An active task untouched this long is STALE. |
| `notPickedUpAfterHours` | integer (at least 1) | `24` | An open task its owner has not touched this long after it was assigned is NOT-PICKED-UP. |
| `prioritySkipAfterHours` | integer (at least 1) | `24` | A session's in-progress task below its own open top-priority task this long is a PRIORITY-SKIP. |
| `maxSelfMadePerDay` | integer (0 to 200) | `10` | A session that added more tasks for itself (created by it, asked by no one else) in the last 24 hours than this is a SELF-MADE in teamrig check; 0 turns the flag off. |
| `goalProgressDays` | integer (0 to 7) | `1` | Whole days (the team's day: wake.dayStartUtc, else UTC) that may end with no goal or week-plan task moved by its owner, while the week has usage left, before a NO-PROGRESS in teamrig check; 0 turns the flag off. |
| `overSizeMultiple` | number (0 to 10) | `2` | An active sized task whose cost, as the budget meter attributes it, passed this many times its size (--size) is OVER-SIZE in teamrig check; 0 turns the flag off. |
| `weekLengthDays` | integer (1 to 31) | `7` | The length, in days, of the week plan teamrig check measures the week's tasks against. |
| `stopgapFiles` | array (at most 20 items) of string (1 to 260 characters) | `["CLAUDE.md",".claude/rules"]` | The files teamrig check scans for stopgap T\<id> tags besides every skill, a STOPGAP-DONE flag for each tag that names a finished task: paths relative to the team's project folder, or absolute; a path ending in .md is one file, any other a folder whose .md files are read. |

## `register.review`

How teamrig asks for a bug's review.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | one of `"refuse"`, `"warn"`, `"off"` | `"refuse"` | A bug (--type bug) reaching a requireOn status with review parts missing (--cause, --how, --prevent, --missed-test, --missed-monitor, --missed-log, and --harden when critical): refuse the change and name the missing flags, warn (make it and print them), or off (ask nothing). |
| `requireOn` | array (at most 2 items) of one of `"verifying"`, `"done"` | `["verifying","done"]` | The statuses a bug cannot reach with review parts missing. A dropped task is never asked: its note says why. |
| `criticalOwners` | array (at most 32 items) of [session name](#shared-types) | `[]` | Sessions whose every bug counts as critical, and so is asked --harden too: a team's security or data areas. |
| `hintPattern` | string (at least 1 character) | `"\\b(fix\|bug\|broken?\|regress\\w*\|incident\|fail\\w*\|crash\\w*\|leak\\w*\|wrong\|missed)\\b"` | A regular expression, matched case-insensitively against the title and description of a task with no type: a match prints a NOTE line asking to mark it --type bug [--critical], or --type task, when the task is added and when it starts. |

## `skills`

The team's Claude Code skills: the shared area prefix, the limits teamrig check holds each skill to, and how a session lists the skills of other areas.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sharedPrefix` | [session name](#shared-types) | `"team"` | The area prefix of skills shared by the whole team. |
| `maxDescriptionWords` | integer (5 to 200) | `30` | A skill whose description runs over this many words is flagged DESCRIPTION. |
| `maxPerArea` | integer (1 to 100) | `8` | An area with more skills than this is flagged AREA-OVER-LIMIT: merge before adding. |
| `maxVerifiedAgeDays` | integer (1 to 365) | `30` | A skill last verified more than this many days ago is flagged UNVERIFIED. |
| `forbidFrontmatter` | array (at most 8 items) of string (at most 32 characters, matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`) | `["allowed-tools"]` | Frontmatter keys a team skill may not set; a skill is never a permission. |
| `otherAreas` | one of `"on"`, `"name-only"`, `"user-invocable-only"`, `"off"` | `"name-only"` | How a session teamrig launches lists a skill of another session's area whose "Used by:" line does not name it: on in full, name-only without its description, user-invocable-only only as a /name command the model is not shown, off not at all. Shared and personal skills are always listed in full. |

## `contextFiles`

Character budgets for the text Claude Code puts in every call's context; teamrig doctor flags a file over its budget.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxClaudeMdChars` | integer (500 to 500000) | `12000` | The CLAUDE.md files a session loads: the user's, and the project folder's and each parent's. |
| `maxMemoryIndexChars` | integer (500 to 500000) | `6000` | The project's memory index (MEMORY.md). |
| `maxSkillListingChars` | integer (500 to 500000) | `4000` | The skill listing: one name: description line per skill. |
| `maxSessionListsChars` | integer (500 to 500000) | `16000` | The lists the newest session's context holds: skills, deferred tools, agent types and MCP server instructions. |

## `lock`

The file lock each write of the team's state files takes (the task list, the exec audit, the GitHub sync), so two writes never interleave.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ttlMs` | integer (at least 1000) | `300000` | The longest, in ms, a holder keeps a lock: one older than this is taken over even while a process with its pid runs, since that pid may be another process's by then. A lock whose process is gone is taken over at once. |
| `pollMs` | integer (at least 10) | `50` | How often, in ms, a waiter retries. |
| `waitMs` | integer (at least 0) | `20000` | How long, in ms, a waiter tries before it gives up. |

## `pushGuard`

The push guard: what a git push to a protected branch does.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `protectedBranches` | array (at most 8 items) of string (at most 64 characters, matching `^[^\s~^:?*[\\]+$`) | `["main","master"]` | The branches the push guard watches: a push to one goes as pushToProtected says; force-push, mirror and deletion are refused. An empty list guards nothing. |
| `pushToProtected` | one of `"ask"`, `"allow"`, `"lead"`, `"gated"` | `"ask"` | A normal push to a protected branch: ask asks the human, allow lets it through with a note, lead lets the lead's own through and another session's once the lead approved its waiting task (teamrig approve), else refuses it with how to ask, never asking the human. gated clears a hand push as lead does, and teamrig merge merges a change that holds the self-merge gates (its own live task, a pass record of the rebased tree, commit sizes, tests with source, the repo's review gate) with no approval, logging it in merges.jsonl, and holds one that misses a gate for its session's leader. Force-push, mirror and deletion stay refused; a --force-with-lease push and a command the guard cannot read still ask. |
| `reviewPaths` | array (at most 128 items) of [object](#pushguardreviewpaths) | `[]` | The team's review gate entries, read on top of teamrig's generic security list (lockfiles, package manager config, git and agent hooks, CI, container files, git attributes), which none removes. A glob with no slash names a file at any depth, one with a slash is read from the repo root; case is ignored. always holds a change touching the path for its class's reviewer; check runs the repo's reviewCheck first. A bad mode or class reads as always and security. |

## `pushGuard.reviewPaths[]`

The team's review gate entries, read on top of teamrig's generic security list (lockfiles, package manager config, git and agent hooks, CI, container files, git attributes), which none removes. A glob with no slash names a file at any depth, one with a slash is read from the repo root; case is ignored. always holds a change touching the path for its class's reviewer; check runs the repo's reviewCheck first. A bad mode or class reads as always and security.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `glob` (required) | string (1 to 200 characters) |  | The paths the entry covers: with no slash a file name at any depth, with one a path from the repo root; case is ignored. |
| `mode` | one of `"always"`, `"check"` | `"always"` | always holds a change touching the paths for the class's reviewer; check runs the repo's reviewCheck first, which clears the change or holds it. |
| `class` | one of `"security"`, `"leader"` | `"security"` | Who reviews a held change: security (roles.securityReviewer), or leader (the session's lead or sub-lead). |

## `exec`

Privileged commands a reviewer approved, run once by teamrig exec run.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | array (at most 16 items) of string (at most 260 characters, matching `^(?:[A-Za-z]:[\\/]\|/)[^;:]*$`) | `[]` | The folders a privileged command's bare program name (teamrig exec) is looked up on, in order, and the only PATH its commands get; the session's own PATH is never searched. Each is absolute (C:/tools, /usr/bin) with no ; or : past the drive. Empty: a request names its program by absolute path. |
| `webhookEnv` | string (matching `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$`) |  | The name of the environment variable holding the webhook URL that every exec approval, refusal and run is posted to, never the URL itself. Absent: nothing is posted; named but unset: each would-be post warns. |

## `packageGuard`

The package guard: what a Bash or PowerShell call that installs a package or runs one ad hoc does.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `adHocRunners` | one of `"deny"`, `"ask"`, `"allow"` | `"deny"` | A Bash or PowerShell call that fetches a package outside the project's lockfile and runs it at once (npx of a tool not in node\_modules/.bin, npm exec, npm create or init \<x>, pnpm dlx, yarn dlx, bunx): deny refuses it, ask asks the human, allow lets it run. |
| `installs` | one of `"deny"`, `"ask"`, `"allow"` | `"deny"` | A Bash or PowerShell call that installs a package version the guard cannot vet (npm install, pnpm add, yarn add, bun add and their updates): a range or a bare update rather than an exact version or tag, a git or URL source, or a version published fewer than cooldownDays ago or with a known advisory. deny refuses it, ask asks the human, allow lets it run. |
| `cooldownDays` | integer (0 to 365) | `14` | A version published fewer days ago than this is not vetted: a fresh release is unproven. 0 vets any age. |

## `commitGuard`

The commit guard: what a Bash or PowerShell call that runs git without the repository's hooks does.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `skipHooks` | one of `"deny"`, `"ask"`, `"allow"` | `"deny"` | A Bash or PowerShell call that runs git without the repository's hooks: --no-verify (or -n for git commit and git am), HUSKY set for it, or a core.hooksPath that -c, a GIT\_CONFIG\* variable or git config sets or unsets: deny refuses it, ask asks the human, allow lets it run. |

## `prompts`

The permission prompts teamrig's own hooks raise.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hookAsks` | one of `"ask"`, `"refuse"` | `"ask"` | A call a teamrig hook would ask the human about (a push to a protected branch or one it cannot read, an ad-hoc package run, a git command without hooks, a call that would print a secret, a helper over the budget, as their own keys set): ask raises the permission prompt; refuse refuses it instead, its reason telling the session to record the step as waiting for the owner's approval and take its next task, so no prompt holds a session while nobody is there to answer it. |

## `secretGuard`

Refuses a Bash, PowerShell, Read or Grep call that would print a secret into the session, where it stays in the transcript and every later prompt: a secret file's content, the whole environment, a secret variable's value, a Kubernetes secret's data or a dump command's output (kubectl config view --raw); and a Bash or PowerShell line that holds a secret as text (a token, credentials in a URL or an Authorization header), as the line itself stays in the transcript; and a Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit whose written text holds one, unless it writes a secret file (paths). A value handed to the tool that needs it (a pipe into docker login --password-stdin, a redirect into a file) stays allowed, and the read-only shell hook never lets such a line run without a prompt.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `secretReads` | one of `"deny"`, `"ask"`, `"allow"` | `"deny"` | A call that would print a secret: cat .env, Get-Content \~/.npmrc, the Read tool on a secret file, env, printenv, Get-ChildItem Env:, echo $GITHUB\_TOKEN, kubectl get secret -o yaml, kubectl config view --raw: deny refuses it, ask asks the human, allow lets it run, which is the owner's call: check flags it (SECRET-GUARD-OFF). |
| `writes` | one of `"deny"`, `"ask"`, `"allow"` | `"deny"` | A call that holds a secret as text: a command line with one in it (curl -H "Authorization: Bearer \<a token>"), or a Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit whose written text holds one outside a secret file (a token written into src/): deny refuses it, ask asks the human, allow lets it run, which is the owner's call: check flags it (SECRET-GUARD-OFF). |
| `paths` | array (at most 32 items) of string (at most 200 characters) | `[]` | The team's own secret files, read after the defaults (\*\*/.env, \*\*/.env.\*, \~/.npmrc, \~/.ssh/\*\*, \~/.aws/credentials, \*\*/.kube/config, \~/.docker/config.json, \*\*/.git-credentials, \~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, \~/.claude/.credentials.json, \~/.claude/history.jsonl, \*\*/.claude/settings.local.json, \~/.bash\_history, \~/.zsh\_history, \*\*/PSReadLine/\*\_history.txt, \*\*/\*.pem, \*\*/\*.key, \*\*/\*.p12, \*\*/\*.pfx, \*\*/\*.jks, \*\*/\*.keystore, \*\*/id\_rsa, \*\*/id\_ecdsa, \*\*/id\_ed25519, \*\*/\*.tfstate, \*\*/\*.tfstate.backup; .env.example, .env.sample and \~/.ssh/\*.pub stay readable). \~/ starts at home, a glob with no leading / or drive matches at any depth, and the last glob that matches a path decides: !glob keeps a path readable. |
| `envNames` | array (at most 16 items) of string (at most 120 characters) | `[]` | The team's own patterns for environment variables whose values are secrets, regular expressions over the name with case ignored, read after the defaults (TOKEN, SECRET, PASSW, PASS, CRED, AUTH except AUTHOR and an auth mechanism or source, PRIVATE, KEY, DSN, WEBHOOK, COOKIE, PAT, SALT, and a store's connection URL or string by its kind: DB\_URL, DATABASE\_URL, PG\_URI, CACHE\_URL, BROKER\_URL, CONNECTION\_STRING). A store named by its product is the team's to add. The last pattern that matches a name decides: !pattern keeps a variable printable. |
| `commands` | array (at most 16 items) of string (at most 200 characters) | `[]` | The team's own commands whose output is a secret whatever file or variable they name, regular expressions over a command's program and arguments with case ignored, read after the default (kubectl config view --raw). The last pattern that matches a command decides: !pattern lets it print. |
| `redact` | boolean | `true` | After a Bash, PowerShell, Read or Grep call runs, replace each secret its result holds (a token by its shape, a match of register.secretPatterns, the value of a secret variable) before the model and the transcript see it, and tell the session which kinds it held and the task filed to rotate each. false shows results whole; turning it off is the owner's call: check flags it (SECRET-GUARD-OFF). |

## `commits`

The small-commits rule: one logical change per commit; a commit over either bound needs a reason line.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxLines` | integer (50 to 5000) | `400` | Changed non-test lines (added + deleted) a commit may carry without a reason line. |
| `maxFiles` | integer (2 to 500) | `15` | Changed non-test files a commit may carry without a reason line. |
| `largeCommitTrailer` | string (matching `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,39}$`) | `"Large-commit"` | The key of the reason line, as in `Large-commit: <reason>`. |
| `testPatterns` | array (at most 8 items) of string (at most 100 characters) | `["(^\|/)(tests?\|__tests__\|spec)/","\\.(test\|spec)\\.[^/]+$","(^\|/)test_[^/]+\\.py$"]` | Regular expressions over /-separated paths; a file that matches one is a test and never counts. |
| `sourcePatterns` | array (at most 8 items) of string (at most 100 characters) | `["\\.([cm]?[jt]sx?\|py\|go\|rs\|java\|kt\|cs\|c\|cc\|cpp\|h\|hpp\|rb\|swift\|vue\|svelte\|sh\|ps1)$"]` | Regular expressions over /-separated paths; a non-test file that matches one is source. A change of source with no test changed misses the self-merge gate (pushGuard.pushToProtected gated). |
| `gate` | one of `"off"`, `"warn"`, `"refuse"` | `"warn"` | A push to a protected branch: off ignores large commits, warn lists them when it asks the human, refuse refuses the push. |

## `coordinator`

The deploy coordinator: teamrig heavy runs one heavy step on the host at a time, under the host lock, teamrig merge merges a branch into its repository's default branch, teamrig deploy deploys it and teamrig claim holds deploys while a session measures; each step is recorded in the ledger.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dir` | string (at least 1 character) |  | The coordinator's folder, which holds its ledger (ledger.jsonl); a relative path is in the team's folder. Unset: deploys in the state folder. |
| `repos` | map from string (matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$`) to [object](#coordinatorrepos) |  | The repositories whose branches teamrig merge merges into their default branch, by name. |
| `heavy` | [object](#coordinatorheavy) |  | The host lock and the limits of one heavy step. |
| `checkTimeoutSeconds` | integer (1 to 600) | `20` | A deploy's check still running after this many seconds is stopped, and the deploy waits. |
| `claims` | [object](#coordinatorclaims) |  | Quiet claims (teamrig claim), which hold deploys of their targets while a session measures them. |
| `windows` | [object](#coordinatorwindows) |  | teamrig windows: when a measurement of a deploy target is clean, between the deploys and heavy steps that disturb it. |
| `wait` | [object](#coordinatorwait) |  | How a coordinator step waits. |
| `schedule` | [object](#coordinatorschedule) |  | When heavy steps and deploys may start on the host. |

## `coordinator.repos.*`

The repositories whose branches teamrig merge merges into their default branch, by name.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mainCheckout` (required) | string (at least 1 character) |  | The repository's main checkout; a branch merges from any worktree of it. A relative path is in the team's folder. |
| `deploysOnPush` | array of string (matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$`) |  | The deploy targets a push to the default branch deploys by itself (a host that builds on push): quiet claims on them hold the merge, and the push is recorded as their deploy. |
| `dependencyGate` | boolean |  | Refuse a branch (merge) or a pushed range (deploy) whose package files need a dependency install, so the main checkout node\_modules, which its worktrees link to, never changes unreviewed; dependencyCheck clears one for merge, and with deploy.dependencyInstall for a deploy. |
| `dependencyCheck` | array (1 to 64 items) of string (at least 1 character) |  | With dependencyGate, what clears a dependency change: a program and its arguments, run without a shell under the host lock with the base package-lock.json in the file TEAMRIG\_BASELINE\_LOCK names (unset when the base has none). teamrig merge runs it in the branch checkout after the rebase and before the push, the default branch its base; teamrig deploy in the main checkout after the pull, its old HEAD the base. Exit 0 lets the change go, anything else refuses it. |
| `reviewGate` | boolean |  | Hold a branch (merge) whose changed paths hit a review entry (teamrig's generic list and pushGuard.reviewPaths) until its reviewer approves it, or reviewCheck clears its check hits. |
| `reviewCheck` | array (1 to 64 items) of string (at least 1 character) |  | With reviewGate, what a check hit runs: a program and its arguments, run without a shell under the host lock in the branch checkout after the rebase, with the base commit in TEAMRIG\_REVIEW\_BASE. Exit 0 clears the change, 3 holds it for the entry's reviewer with the findings it prints, anything else for that reviewer too. Unset: a check hit is held like an always one. |
| `followMainCheckout` | boolean |  | After the push, fast-forward the main checkout to it: only a fast-forward, only on the default branch with no tracked changes. |
| `worktreeFolder` | string (at least 1 character) | `".claude/worktrees"` | The folder teamrig worktree add makes each new worktree in, one folder per branch named after it with each / as -. A relative path is in the main checkout. |
| `worktreeSetup` | array (1 to 64 items) of string (at least 1 character) |  | What teamrig worktree add runs in a new worktree, such as a link to the main checkout node\_modules: a program and its arguments, run without a shell, with the main checkout folder in TEAMRIG\_MAIN\_CHECKOUT. Anything but exit 0 leaves the worktree in place and fails the add. Unset: nothing runs. |
| `merge` | [object](#coordinatorreposmerge) |  | How teamrig merge merges a branch through the team's own flow, such as a pull request the forge merges. Unset: it pushes the branch to the default branch. |
| `deploy` | [object](#coordinatorreposdeploy) |  | How teamrig deploy deploys what merged into the default branch, each command a program and its arguments run without a shell from the main checkout. Unset: the repository is not deployed. |

## `coordinator.repos.*.merge`

How teamrig merge merges a branch through the team's own flow, such as a pull request the forge merges. Unset: it pushes the branch to the default branch.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` (required) | array (1 to 64 items) of string (at least 1 character) |  | A program and its arguments, run without a shell in the branch checkout under the host lock after the rebase and the dependency check, with TEAMRIG\_MERGE\_BRANCH, TEAMRIG\_MERGE\_BASE (the default branch), TEAMRIG\_MERGE\_HEAD and TEAMRIG\_SESSION set. Exit 0: the branch merged, which teamrig merge confirms on the remote; 75: it waits (say a pull request waits on its checks or review), and running teamrig merge again finishes it once it merges; anything else fails it. Its last output line is shown as the reason. |
| `remote` | string (matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$`) | `"origin"` | The git remote whose default branch the command merges into: teamrig merge rebases onto it, confirms the merge on it and moves the local default branch to it. Set upstream where origin is a contributor's fork; the branch itself is pushed to and deleted from origin either way. |

## `coordinator.repos.*.deploy`

How teamrig deploy deploys what merged into the default branch, each command a program and its arguments run without a shell from the main checkout. Unset: the repository is not deployed.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `targets` | array of string (matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$`) |  | The deploy targets it deploys: quiet claims on them hold it. |
| `checks` | array (at most 16 items) of [object](#coordinatorreposdeploychecks) |  | Checks asked in order before the host lock and again under it; the first that does not pass holds the deploy. Exit 0 lets it go, 75 makes it wait, 2 refuses it; anything else, or no answer within checkTimeoutSeconds, makes it wait. |
| `dependencyInstall` | array (1 to 64 items) of string (at least 1 character) |  | Installs a pulled range's dependency change (package-lock.json, or package.json fields an install reads), such as npm ci --ignore-scripts: run after the pull and the dependencyCheck, before afterPull. A failed install moves the main checkout back and runs again to restore its dependencies. With dependencyGate, a dependency change deploys only when this and dependencyCheck are set. |
| `afterPull` | array (at most 16 items) of array (1 to 64 items) of string (at least 1 character) |  | Run in order after the pull, before command; one that fails ends the deploy before its command runs. |
| `command` (required) | array (1 to 64 items) of string (at least 1 character) |  | Deploys what the pull brought: exit 0 deployed (a stdout line no-deploy: nothing needed deploying), else failed. Its last stdout line is the ledger note. |

## `coordinator.repos.*.deploy.checks[]`

Checks asked in order before the host lock and again under it; the first that does not pass holds the deploy. Exit 0 lets it go, 75 makes it wait, 2 refuses it; anything else, or no answer within checkTimeoutSeconds, makes it wait.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` (required) | string (matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$`) |  | Names the check in a wait or refusal. |
| `command` (required) | array (1 to 64 items) of string (at least 1 character) |  | The check: a program and its arguments. |

## `coordinator.heavy`

The host lock and the limits of one heavy step.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lockPath` | string (at least 1 character) |  | The host lock file every heavy step takes; a relative path is in the team's folder. Unset: host.lock in the kit home, one lock for every team on the host. |
| `lockTtlMinutes` | integer (11 to 1440) | `150` | A taken host lock lasts this many minutes; past it, or once its process is gone, another step takes it over. |
| `maxRunMinutes` | integer (1 to 1430) | `45` | A heavy step still running after this many minutes is killed with every process it started. At most lockTtlMinutes less 10. |
| `smallMaxRunMinutes` | integer (1 to 1430) | `10` | A small step (heavy --small) still running after this many minutes is killed the same way, so a hung one does not hold back the steps waiting for the lock; a longer step runs without --small. At most maxRunMinutes. |
| `waitMinutes` | integer (0 to 1440) | `60` | A heavy step is refused once its line for the host lock has not moved for this many minutes: no step ahead of it, holding the lock or sharing the host ended meanwhile. |
| `memorySampleSeconds` | integer (0 to 600) | `15` | While a heavy step runs, its process tree's memory and the host's free memory are sampled this often, for its ledger record's peakTreeMb and lowFreeMb; 0 samples nothing. |
| `memoryFloorMb` | integer (0 to 1048576) | `4096` | A small step (heavy --small) shares the host only while it keeps this many MB free besides those held for the small steps. |
| `smallReserveMb` | integer (0 to 1048576) | `2048` | The MB held for a small step with no ledger record of its peak yet. |

## `coordinator.claims`

Quiet claims (teamrig claim), which hold deploys of their targets while a session measures them.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxMinutes` | integer (1 to 1440) | `120` | A claim lasts at most this many minutes. |

## `coordinator.windows`

teamrig windows: when a measurement of a deploy target is clean, between the deploys and heavy steps that disturb it.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `settleMinutes` | integer (0 to 1440) | `30` | A target measures cleanly this many minutes after a deploy reached it. |
| `targetSettleMinutes` | map from string to integer (0 to 1440) |  | Per deploy target, its own settle minutes in place of settleMinutes; each a target some repository deploys. |
| `assumedDeployMinutes` | integer (0 to 1440) | `20` | How long a deploy is taken to have run before its ledger.md line when the ledger has no record of its start. |
| `minMinutes` | integer (1 to 1440) | `15` | The shortest clean window worth listing. |

## `coordinator.wait`

How a coordinator step waits.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pollSeconds` | integer (1 to 600) | `30` | A waiting step looks again after this many seconds; the first in line for the host lock every 2 at most. |
| `maxMinutes` | integer (0 to 1440) | `60` | A deploy step (teamrig merge, deploy) waits this many minutes at most for quiet claims and the host lock, then is refused; a wait in a line for the lock that keeps moving goes on past them. |

## `coordinator.schedule`

When heavy steps and deploys may start on the host.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resetBlackoutHours` | integer (1 to 48) |  | No deploy (teamrig merge) starts from this many hours before the weekly token reset until the reset. Unset: no blackout. |
| `heavyCutoffUtc` | string (matching `^([01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$`) |  | No heavy step starts on the host after this UTC time until midnight. |

## `budget`

The weekly token budget: the pace line the team is measured against and each session's daily part of it. Usage is in weighted tokens (W) read from the session transcripts, and in % of the week from the status line when there is one. The defaults only measure and show; nothing blocks or acts.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns on the live warning and the core rules' pacing sentence; teamrig budget shows usage either way. |
| `account` | string (1 to 100 characters, matching `^[^\r\n]+$`) |  | The Claude account the team's week is on: teams with the same account share one week and split its daily budget. Unset: the Claude config dir, since one config dir signs in one account. |
| `weeklyLimitW` | integer (1000000 to 1000000000000) |  | The weekly limit in weighted tokens. Unset: derived from the status line's weekly %. |
| `subagentWeight` | number (0.1 to 10) | `1` | What one W of a subagent's transcript costs against the weekly limit, in W of a main session. The meter multiplies each subagent call's W by it, so weeklyLimitW is in main-session W. 1: both cost alike. |
| `extraWPerUsd` | integer (1000 to 1000000000) |  | W per US dollar of extra usage, standing in until two spent readings past 100% of the week teach the rate. Unset: the extra-usage pool shows in dollars only until then, with no allowance. |
| `reset` | [object](#budgetreset) |  | When the weekly limit resets, for a team without a status line. Unset: the reset time the status line reports. |
| `targetPct` | number (1 to 100) | `99.5` | Use the week up to this share of the weekly limit. |
| `reservePct` | number (0 to 50) | `0.5` | Kept back for incidents until shortly before the reset; targetPct plus reservePct is at most 100. |
| `paceEndHoursBeforeReset` | number (0 to 48) | `1` | The pace line reaches targetPct this many hours before the reset. |
| `sessions` | map from [session name](#shared-types) to [object](#budgetsessions) | `{}` | Each session's weight in the split of the team's daily budget, by id: its part is the budget × share × its queued work / the sum over the sessions, recomputed at every reading. A session not listed has a share of 1. |
| `pauseByPriority` | boolean | `false` | On a short day, when what is left of the week gives less than the pace line plans for the day, fund the team's sessions' queued work in priority order (p0 first, idle sessions last) and pause the sessions none of it reaches, so the top work keeps its pace. The lead, the coordinator owner held in the team and lifted sessions are never paused. Off: no session of the team is paused. |
| `warnAtPct` | array (at most 8 items) of number (1 to 1000) | `[80,100]` | The live warning shows a line as a session passes each of these % of its daily budget. |
| `paceTolerancePct` | number (0 to 10) | `0.5` | The team is ahead of its pace line once its used % is more than this many points above it. |
| `overAction` | one of `"warn"`, `"ask-lead"`, `"ask"`, `"block"` | `"warn"` | Past a session's daily budget: warn shows the lines only; ask-lead also writes the lead an inbox line; ask also asks the person before a helper launch; block refuses helper launches. |
| `escalate` | one of `"session"`, `"session-and-fleet"` | `"session-and-fleet"` | When an action beyond the lines applies: session when the session is over its budget; session-and-fleet only when the team is also ahead of its pace line. |
| `quietHours` | [object](#budgetquiethours) |  | UTC hours in which the live warning applies action on its own, while the team sleeps. Unset: none. |
| `lift` | [object](#budgetlift) |  | Bounds on a leader's lift of a session's or a sub-lead's group's daily budget (teamrig budget lift). Every lift carries a stop %, the share of the week at which it ends. |
| `statusSnapshotDir` | string (at least 1 character) |  | The folder of status line snapshots, \<Claude session id>.json each. Unset: \<kit home>/usage/live. |
| `maxBytesPerHook` | integer (100000 to 100000000) | `4000000` | The most transcript bytes one hook run reads; the rest waits for the next run. |

## `budget.reset`

When the weekly limit resets, for a team without a status line. Unset: the reset time the status line reports.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `weekday` (required) | one of `"sun"`, `"mon"`, `"tue"`, `"wed"`, `"thu"`, `"fri"`, `"sat"` |  | The day the weekly limit resets. |
| `timeUtc` (required) | string (matching `^([01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$`) |  | The time it resets, HH:MM UTC. |

## `budget.sessions.*`

Each session's weight in the split of the team's daily budget, by id: its part is the budget × share × its queued work / the sum over the sessions, recomputed at every reading. A session not listed has a share of 1.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `share` | number (0 to 100) | `1` | The session's weight in the split, as sessions describes it. |

## `budget.quietHours`

UTC hours in which the live warning applies action on its own, while the team sleeps. Unset: none.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `startUtc` (required) | string (matching `^([01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$`) |  | Where the quiet hours start, HH:MM UTC. |
| `endUtc` (required) | string (matching `^([01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$`) |  | Where they end, HH:MM UTC; an end before the start runs them past midnight. |
| `action` (required) | one of `"warn"`, `"ask-lead"`, `"ask"`, `"block"` |  | What the live warning does in the quiet hours, with overAction's choices. |
| `paceWeight` | number (0 to 1) |  | What a quiet minute counts on the pace line and in the daily budget, against 1 for any other minute. 0 when unset: the team sleeps, so the line stays flat through the night. |

## `budget.lift`

Bounds on a leader's lift of a session's or a sub-lead's group's daily budget (teamrig budget lift). Every lift carries a stop %, the share of the week at which it ends.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxStopPct` | number (1 to 100) | `99.3` | The highest stop % a lift may carry. |
| `reserveStopPct` | number (1 to 100) | `99.9` | The highest stop % of a --reserve lift, given only in the last hour before the reset; it ends 15 minutes before the reset. Never below maxStopPct. |

## `leadBoundary`

How teamrig keeps the lead leading: its own edits, tests and code searches are nudged and shown, never blocked.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Off: the lead's own edits, tests and code searches are neither nudged nor shown. |
| `ownPaths` | array (at most 16 items) of string (at most 256 characters) | `[]` | The lead's own files and folders beyond the team's teamrig folder and Claude Code's memory folders, which always count: editing or searching them is its job. \~ is the user's home, \* one folder name. |
| `searchNudgeAt` | integer (0 to 50) | `3` | The turn's code search (a source-file Read, a Grep, a Glob or a shell search outside the lead's own paths) that brings the lead one nudge, and from which the owner's turn-end line counts searches; 0 never. |

## `loops`

Loop discipline inside a turn.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chainNudgeAt` | integer (0 to 50) | `3` | After this many single-tool calls in a row in one turn, the session gets one line asking it to send independent steps as several tool calls in one message, and an edit with its re-test; 0 never asks. |

## `wake`

Waking a session idle at its prompt when work is handed to it, instead of at its next prompt. Only work the session can go on with wakes (open or started past every task it comes after, or waiting with every wait cleared or answered), tasks handed together wake once, and each wake says what it costs.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Off: a session sees new work only at its next prompt. |
| `priority` | integer (1 to 99) | `1` | The least urgent priority that wakes a session: 1 wakes for p0 and p1 only. A session its budget holds (past its daily budget while the team has no room today, the wake's own turn counted for both) wakes for p0 only, and one in the budget's quiet hours for p0 and p1 only, whatever this says. |
| `batchSeconds` | integer (0 to 3600) | `120` | How long a wake waits after the first new task it is for, so tasks handed together wake the session once. |
| `minGapMinutes` | integer (0 to 1440) | `15` | The least time between two wakes of one session; work handed meanwhile waits and wakes it once. |
| `dayStartUtc` | string (matching `^([01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$`) |  | The day's start (HH:MM UTC, outside the budget's quiet hours): from then each session with work it can start, of any priority, that has had no turn since gets one wake that day, and a burst wakes its sessions the same way once it starts. Unset: no day-start wake, and a burst wakes no one. |

## `tests`

What teamrig test prints of a failed run.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxFailureChars` | integer (500 to 50000) | `4000` | The most characters of failing tests teamrig test prints after a failed run, all of them together; the rest stays in its log. |

## `github`

teamrig gh sync: GitHub issues read into the register as tasks of source github. It only reads GitHub and never writes to it; local tasks stay local. Each owner's repositories are read with the read-only token saved as teamrig-gh-\<owner> in the system's credential store, else the gh login (docs/github-sync.md).

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repos` | array (at most 20 items) of string (at most 140 characters, matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}$`) | `[]` | The repositories to read, as owner/name; matched without case. Empty turns the import off. |
| `owners` | map from string (matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}$`) to [session name](#shared-types) | `{}` | The session that owns an issue assigned to each GitHub login; matched without case. An issue with no listed assignee goes to its repository's session in sessions, else the lead. |
| `sessions` | map from string (matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38}/[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,100}$`) to [session name](#shared-types) | `{}` | The session that owns the issues of each repository (owner/name, one of repos; matched without case) when none of their assignees is in owners. Without one, they go to the lead. |
| `closedDays` | integer (1 to 365) | `14` | How many days back closed issues are read, to finish the tasks they were imported as. |
| `everyMinutes` | integer (0 to 1440) | `15` | How often the hooks start a sync on their own, in minutes, once for the whole team; 0 leaves it to teamrig gh sync --yes. |

## `alerts`

The alerting rule the core rules state.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `persistentFailureHours` | integer (1 to 720) | `24` | The same external failure for this long must page a human. |

## `decisions`

When the lead asks the owner the decisions waiting on them (tasks waiting on the owner's decision or approval), together in one batch instead of one at a time. A batch holds the waits not yet asked and the asked ones now past their due date; `teamrig decisions` prints it and `teamrig decisions asked` records it asked, as a meeting's start does. The lead's check says when one is due.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `batchTimesUtc` | array (at most 8 items) of string (matching `^([01]\d\|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$`) | `[]` | The lead's batch times, HH:MM UTC (its budget checkpoints, say): a batch is due once one passed since the last was asked. A wait due before the next batch time is asked at once. With none, a batch comes only at the daily meeting or by batchAt, and a wait due within a day is asked at once. |
| `batchAt` | integer (0 to 50) | `5` | A batch is due once this many waits on the owner are not yet asked; 0: never by count. |
| `askWith` | one of `"text"`, `"picker"` | `"text"` | How the lead asks the owner each decision at the daily meeting: text reads the cards in plain text and the owner answers in their own words; picker asks the choices with Claude Code's question picker (AskUserQuestion), at most 4 a call. With pickerGuard on, the picker opens for the lead in the meeting only under picker. |

## `tabStatus`

A colored circle before each terminal tab's title for what its session is doing: green ready, yellow working (or a helper still running), orange waiting on the user, blue waiting on the user's decision (a turn whose last message has a `Decision needed:` line), red an API error, purple compacting.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Shows the circle in every tab of the team; team create turns it on in a new team's config. It also needs CLAUDE\_CODE\_DISABLE\_TERMINAL\_TITLE=1 in Claude Code's environment, else Claude Code writes its own title over it. |

## `pickerGuard`

Refuses Claude Code's question picker (AskUserQuestion) in every session and helper of the team, and in the lead's own thread unless the owner's daily meeting is open: the picker stops the session until the person answers, and the owner may be away for hours, so none of its other tasks moves meanwhile. The refusal tells the session to decide it when it is its own, else to record it on its task (a waiting status with its decision card, --default included), which reaches the owner through the lead, and go on with its next task; only with no task left, to end its turn with the question and a `Decision needed:` line. A helper ends its report with the decision instead. Plan mode's ExitPlanMode stays allowed.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Refuses the question picker in every session and helper of the team, and in the lead's own thread outside the owner's daily meeting. |

## `turnLog`

Each session's prompts and replies, kept in state/turn-log/\<session>/\<UTC hour>.jsonl for the task pane, so a /clear or a compaction never takes away what the person was reading in the tab. Secret shapes are redacted.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Off: nothing is written. |
| `keepHours` | integer (1 to 168) | `24` | How long each entry is kept, in hours; whole hours past it are removed at a session start. |

## `readonlyShell`

Lets a Bash or PowerShell line run without a permission prompt when every command in it provably only reads: known readers (grep, cat, Get-Content, Select-Object...), git and kubectl reading subcommands, and no write, file redirection, command that runs code, or variable a program reads. It only ever allows: any other line gets Claude Code's own permission check.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Turns the hook on for every session of the team. |
| `allowPrefixes` | array (at most 16 items) of string (at most 120 characters, matching `^[\w@./:+][\w@./:+-]*(?: [\w@./:=+-]+)*$`) | `[]` | Commands trusted with any arguments, each by its leading words, such as "npx tsc --noEmit" or "npx jest". The hook cannot read what they do, so a prefix vouches for every argument after it: leave out a tool whose flags write (eslint --fix, jest -u). |

## `permissions`

Which local allow rules stay. An allow rule in a Claude Code settings file approves a call before auto mode's classifier sees it, so a rule that approves a whole tool or a program with any arguments skips the one check that stops an injected or mistaken action. teamrig permissions trim removes the rules off keepAllow (the owner runs it with --yes); doctor flags the ones that approve a whole tool or program, or hold a credential (text in a secret's shape) that Claude Code saved with an approved command.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keepAllow` | array (at most 64 items) of string (at most 120 characters, matching `^[A-Za-z][\w-]*(?:\([^*/\\()\r\n]+(?: \*\|:\*)?\))?$`) | `["Bash(kubectl get *)","PowerShell(kubectl get *)","Bash(kubectl describe *)","PowerShell(kubectl describe *)","Bash(kubectl logs *)","PowerShell(kubectl logs *)","Bash(kubectl top *)","PowerShell(kubectl top *)","Bash(kubectl rollout status *)","PowerShell(kubectl rollout status *)","Bash(kubectl version *)","PowerShell(kubectl version *)","Bash(kubectl config current-context *)","PowerShell(kubectl config current-context *)","Bash(npm ls *)","PowerShell(npm ls *)","Bash(npm view *)","PowerShell(npm view *)","Bash(gh pr view *)","PowerShell(gh pr view *)","Bash(gh pr list *)","PowerShell(gh pr list *)","Bash(gh pr checks *)","PowerShell(gh pr checks *)","Bash(gh run list *)","PowerShell(gh run list *)","Bash(gh run view *)","PowerShell(gh run view *)","Bash(tasklist *)","PowerShell(tasklist *)","Bash(netstat *)","PowerShell(netstat *)","Bash(sleep *)","PowerShell(sleep *)","PowerShell(Test-Path *)","PowerShell(Get-Date *)","PowerShell(Get-Process *)","WebSearch"]` | Rules kept as they are, such as "Bash(kubectl get \*)" or "WebSearch": a tool, or a tool and a command with at most a trailing " \*" or ":\*" (read as the same). A kept "Tool(x \*)" also keeps "Tool(x)", and a shell rule's leading "MSYS\_NO\_PATHCONV=1 " reads as absent. Keep only commands whose arguments can neither run a program nor write. The default is the general part of security's list of read-only commands outside Claude Code's own read-only set; a team's list replaces it, so one that adds its own tools' read-only commands repeats the default's. |

## `open`

How teamrig open starts a session in a new terminal tab.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `terminal` | one of `"auto"`, `"tmux"`, `"windows-terminal"`, `"macos-terminal"`, `"gnome-terminal"`, `"konsole"`, `"x-terminal-emulator"`, `"print"` | `"auto"` | The terminal to open the tab in. auto takes tmux inside tmux, else Windows Terminal on Windows, Terminal on macOS, or the first of gnome-terminal, konsole and x-terminal-emulator on Linux; print opens nothing and prints the command to run. teamrig open --terminal wins over it. |
| `teamWindow` | boolean | `false` | Opens each tab of the team's sessions (teamrig open, a meeting start, a refresh restart, the idle pass's reopen and a restore after a reboot) in a Windows Terminal window of the team's own, named teamrig-\<team>, made when none is open, so each team's tabs stay apart from other teams'. Off opens them in the most recent window. Other terminals open as before. |
| `headroom` | [object](#openheadroom) |  | The room teamrig open and teamrig hire --yes need on the host before they add a session: free memory over coordinator.heavy.memoryFloorMb with the session, and the commit charge within commitMaxPct. The lead opens whatever the room. |
| `idle` | [object](#openidle) |  | The idle pass: it would close a session the wake check would not wake once it has been quiet open.headroom.closeIdleMinutes, and reopen it when the wake check would wake it. The lead and the coordinator owner are never closed. |

## `open.headroom`

The room teamrig open and teamrig hire --yes need on the host before they add a session: free memory over coordinator.heavy.memoryFloorMb with the session, and the commit charge within commitMaxPct. The lead opens whatever the room.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sessionMb` | integer (100 to 65536) | `1200` | The MB a new session is counted to need while no session runs to measure; else the median running session's Claude Code process tree. |
| `commitMaxPct` | integer (50 to 100) | `92` | The most of the host's commit limit, in %, its commit charge may reach with the new session counted (Windows and Linux; elsewhere free memory alone is checked). |
| `closeIdleMinutes` | integer (15 to 10080) | `60` | How long, in minutes, a session stays quiet before teamrig close may end it to free the host; teamrig open resumes it. |

## `open.idle`

The idle pass: it would close a session the wake check would not wake once it has been quiet open.headroom.closeIdleMinutes, and reopen it when the wake check would wake it. The lead and the coordinator owner are never closed.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | one of `"off"`, `"dry-run"`, `"on"` | `"on"` | off runs no pass; dry-run runs it and logs each close or reopen it would make, with its reason, and makes none; on, the default, also starts each of those closes and reopens, hidden, and logs its outcome. |
| `keepOpen` | array of [session name](#shared-types) | `[]` | Sessions the idle pass and teamrig close never close for being quiet, on top of the lead and the coordinator owner. |

## `statusLine`

What teamrig statusline shows beside the model and the plan's use of the week.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `folder` | boolean | `true` | The name of the session's folder. |
| `branch` | boolean | `true` | The branch checked out there, or the commit of a detached HEAD. |
| `resume` | boolean | `true` | The command that resumes the session: claude --resume \<session id>. |

## `launch.*`

Each session's Claude Code model and effort, and the folder it works in, by id: teamrig open starts it with claude --model and --effort; a session running on another model is told the /model to type at its start, and one at another effort the /effort to type at its first stop. A model or effort left unset is Claude Code's own choice, except for the lead, which starts on model opus at xhigh effort for each one it leaves unset.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | one of `"default"`, `"best"`, `"fable"`, `"opus"`, `"sonnet"`, `"haiku"`, `"opusplan"`, `"fable[1m]"`, `"opus[1m]"`, `"sonnet[1m]"`, `"opusplan[1m]"` or string (at most 100 characters, matching `^claude-[a-z0-9]+(?:[.@-][a-z0-9]+)*(?:\[1m\])?$`) |  | A Claude Code model alias or a full model id such as claude-opus-5-5. best is Fable where the account has it, else Opus; default leaves the model to Claude Code. |
| `effort` | one of `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"xhigh"`, `"max"` |  | The effort level; a model that lacks it runs at the highest level it has below it. |
| `project` | string |  | The session's project folder, an absolute path: teamrig open starts it there, and close and hire look for its Claude Code sessions there. Unset, team.project, else the folder holding the team's .teamrig.json pointer; doctor flags a folder that does not exist. |

## `refresh`

Context refresh: when a session finishes a task (teamrig set \<id> --status done) with its context at or over contextTokens, or with everyTasks tasks finished since its context was last fresh and the context at everyTasksMinTokens or more, or after the lead ran teamrig refresh \<session>, it writes a handover; then the user types /clear, or teamrig starts it fresh on its own (autoRestart). A relative handoverDir is resolved against the team's folder; unset, it is \<team folder>/handover.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | Off: no session is asked for a handover or refreshed. |
| `contextTokens` | integer (10000 to 10000000) | `120000` | The context size, in tokens, that asks for a refresh: under the about 167k where Claude Code compacts a 200k window. |
| `everyTasks` | integer (0 to 100) | `3` | Also refresh once this many tasks were finished since the context was last fresh (a /clear, a new process or a compaction); 0 turns it off. |
| `everyTasksMinTokens` | integer (10000 to 10000000) | `80000` | The smallest context, in tokens, the task count refreshes at. |
| `tabTitle` | boolean | `true` | Title the tab once the handover is written: '[\<team>] \<name>: restarting', or '[\<team>] \<name>: type /clear'. |
| `autoRestart` | boolean | `false` | Once the handover is written and the turn has ended, start the session fresh on its own, which reads the handover: the plugin's mod runs /clear in its tab; where no mod claims the ask, teamrig ends its Claude Code and starts it again, in the same tab when teamrig open started it, else in a new tab. A session with no work it can start then waits for a wake that brings it some, which starts it fresh instead of waking it. A prompt typed before then keeps the context. false (the default): the user types /clear once done with the screen, which a /clear wipes. |
| `restartDelaySeconds` | integer (5 to 600) | `15` | How long after the turn's end the automatic restart waits, so the user can still type to keep the context. |
| `holdAfterActivityMinutes` | integer (0 to 60) | `5` | The plugin's mod holds the automatic /clear while the person typed in the tab's prompt (a key, a paste) or sent a prompt there this recently, and while the prompt holds a draft: a /clear never lands under the person. 0: only a draft holds it. |
| `countdownSeconds` | integer (0 to 120) | `20` | Before the plugin's mod runs the automatic /clear, a band above the prompt counts down this many seconds, with Refresh now and Hold 10 min; a key in the prompt holds it too. 0: no count, the /clear runs once nothing else holds it. |
| `compactCeilingTokens` | integer (0 to 10000000) | `185000` | While a session's handover is asked for or written, the plugin's mod stops Claude Code's own compaction (trigger auto) of its main conversation as long as its context, as Claude Code estimates it, is under this many tokens: the /clear at the turn's end replaces it. Past it a compaction goes through; /compact and a subagent's own compaction are never stopped. 0: never stopped. It also bounds the owner's open daily meeting, which holds the lead's refresh only under it; 0 holds it until the meeting ends. |
| `handoverMaxBytes` | integer (0 to 1000000) | `20000` | teamrig refresh --ready refuses a handover larger than this many bytes: the fresh start reads all of it, so a handover that grows section by section fills the next session's context before its work begins. 0: no cap. |
| `endCommand` | array (at most 16 items) of string (at least 1 character) | `[]` | A program (its path, then its arguments) run after an automatic restart ended a session, given Claude Code's SessionEnd hook input (reason clear) on stdin: for a SessionEnd hook the end skipped, since on Windows a process is ended without running them. Empty: none. |
| `handoverDir` | string (at least 1 character) |  | The folder of the sessions' handovers, \<session>.md each; a relative path is in the team's folder. Unset: handover in the team's folder. |

## `hiring`

Hiring sessions with teamrig hire, each a worker the leader is sure the team needs: who decides. No cap counts hires: the host's room bounds who is at the office, and the leader decides who is hired. A hire is written into sessions, names and launch, and logged with its reason and review date; its part of the team's daily budget follows its share and queued work, like any session's.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy` | one of `"off"`, `"owner"`, `"lead"`, `"automatic"` | `"owner"` | off: no hires. owner: a lead (the lead, or a sub-lead into its own group) hires once the owner approved (--approved-by, kept with the hire). lead: a lead hires. automatic: as lead, and a hired session whose last open task closes is asked to write its handover. Under every policy only a lead over a session retires it (teamrig retire). |
| `reviewDays` | integer (1 to 90) | `7` | Days from a hire to its review date, unless teamrig hire --review names one. |
| `resumeMaxTokens` | integer (10000 to 1000000) | `250000` | The most context tokens a rehired session's last Claude Code session may hold for teamrig open --resume to resume it; past it the session starts fresh on its handover. |
| `resumeMaxIdleDays` | integer (1 to 90) | `7` | The most days a rehired session's last Claude Code session may have gone unwritten for teamrig open --resume to resume it; past it the session starts fresh on its handover. |
| `scaleOut` | [object](#hiringscaleout) |  | How teamrig check measures an area against its dated work for a SCALE-OUT flag: its pace is the tasks it finished lately, and the dated tasks of the top priorities are what it must finish in time. |

## `hiring.scaleOut`

How teamrig check measures an area against its dated work for a SCALE-OUT flag: its pace is the tasks it finished lately, and the dated tasks of the top priorities are what it must finish in time.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `windowDays` | integer (1 to 8) | `7` | Days back over which the tasks an area finished give its pace; at most the 8 days a register keeps finished tasks. |
| `minDone` | integer (1 to 100) | `3` | The fewest tasks an area must have finished in that window for its pace to count; below it the area is not measured. |
| `topPriorities` | integer (1 to 10) | `2` | How many of the top priorities count: their dated tasks are the work an area must finish in time. |

## `burst`

Bursts with teamrig burst: a time-boxed scale-out onto helpers and hired sessions that spends more of the week, for a surplus the week would leave unused at the reset or for a deadline. A person always starts one by command; nothing starts one on its own.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy` | one of `"off"`, `"owner"`, `"lead"` | `"owner"` | off: no bursts. owner: the lead starts one once the owner approved (--approved-by, kept with the burst). lead: the lead starts one within the caps. |
| `surplusHours` | integer (1 to 167) | `48` | A surplus burst starts at the earliest this many hours before the week's reset. |
| `minSparePct` | number (0.1 to 100) | `5` | The least share of the week, in %, projected unused at the pace end (at the week's mean rate so far) for a surplus burst; with other teams on the Claude account, the team's part of it (split by weight, as the daily budget is). |
| `maxHelpers` | integer (0 to 20) | `3` | The most helpers each burst session runs at once; the burst's model line states it. |
| `maxHires` | integer (0 to 20) | `2` | The most sessions one burst may hire (teamrig hire --burst). |

## `paths`

Folders moved from their defaults; a relative path is resolved against the team's folder (\<kit home>/teams/\<team>). Unset, state and inbox stay under the team's folder and skills is the skills folder of Claude Code's folder ($CLAUDE\_CONFIG\_DIR, else \~/.claude).

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | string (at least 1 character) |  | The team's state folder: the task list's log, the inboxes, the coordinator's ledger and the logs. Unset: state in the team's folder. |
| `inbox` | string (at least 1 character) |  | The folder of the sessions' inbox files. Unset: inbox in the state folder. |
| `skills` | string (at least 1 character) |  | The Claude Code skills folder teamrig check and doctor read. Unset: skills in Claude Code's folder ($CLAUDE\_CONFIG\_DIR, else \~/.claude). |

| Name | Type | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| session name | string (matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`) |  |
| role holder | string (matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}(/[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31})?$`) | A session of the team by id, or `<team>/<id>`: the session holding the same role on a team above it (doctor's tree-role problem when that team is not above, or the session does not hold the role there). |
